chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated from al-Saffar and Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari, all together, from Yaqub ibn Yazid al-Anbari, from some of his companions, who said:

Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) passed away, and with Ziyad al-Qandi were seventy thousand dinars, and with Uthman ibn Isa al-Rawasi were thirty thousand dinars and five slave girls, and his residence was in Egypt. So Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent to them: 'Carry over to me what is in your possession from the wealth and what has accumulated for my father with you from furniture and slave girls, for I am his heir and the one standing in his place, and we have divided his inheritance, and you have no excuse for withholding what has accumulated for me and his heir while you were holding it,' and words similar to this. As for Ibn Abi Hamza, he denied it and did not acknowledge what he had, and likewise Ziyad al-Qandi. But as for Uthman ibn Isa, he wrote to him: 'Your father (peace be upon him) has not died; he is alive and established, and whoever mentions that he died is a denier [of the truth]. And I act upon the fact that he has passed away as you say, so he did not command me to hand over anything to you, and as for the slave girls, I have emancipated them and married them.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida handle the financial deposits of his father Imam al-Sadiq among his companions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the theological dispute of the Waqifiyya sect, who claimed Imam al-Sadiq had died without appointing a successor. The narrative highlights the practical implications of this belief: Uthman ibn Isa, holding the Imam's wealth, argued that since the Imam was 'dead' (in the sense of the Waqifiyya view), he had already exercised his authority to emancipate and marry the slave girls, thereby justifying his retention of the assets rather than returning them to the rightful heir, Imam al-Rida.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 67 - Muhammad bin Hasan Walid has narrated from Saffar and Saad bin Abdullah Ashari, all together from Yaqub bin Yazid Ambari from some scholars, who said:

When Abu Ibrahim (a.s) passed away, Ziyad Qandi was having seventy thousand dinars with him and Uthman bin Isa Rawasi had thirty thousand dinars and five slave girls and he lived in Egypt. Imam Ali Ridha (a.s) sent a message to them: That which is deposited with you from the wealth of my father and that which you hold from cash and slave girls and other things, send it all to me as I am his successor and I will distribute the inheritance of the Imam. [It is a hint that I know what amount you are having]. You don’t any more have any excuse for keeping that which is deposited with you and from his inheritance; and he issued such commands. But Ibn Abi Hamza originally denied and did not admit having that, which was in his possession. Same was the case of Ziyad Qandi. But Uthman bin Isa wrote to Imam Ridha (a.s): Your father (a.s) is alive and established; and one who believes in his death is having false beliefs. If you say since he is dead, I should act on it [and accept his death], he did not instruct me to hand over anything to you [this was with regard to cash] and as for the slave girls, I have emancipated them and taken them as wives.
